title: The 75% That Nobody Measured: A Pre-Registered Pilot Audit of the Gyushi–Ashtanga Claim Dies at Its Own Reliability Gate
description: A widely repeated claim holds that "~75% of the Gyushi (rGyud bzhi, the Tibetan Four Tantras) comes from the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdayasaṃhitā" — the foundational Ayurvedic compendium of Vāgbhaṭa. The lab's Citation Tracer could find no source for that figure: no method, no codebook, no dataset stands behind it in the indexed literature. It is a zombie statistic. This paper reports a pre-registered attempt to replace it with a measurement — and reports that the attempt failed at its own gate, before any estimate was produced. A 30-chapter pilot (the Explanatory Tantra, the part of the Gyushi where Indian influence is most plausible a priori) was coded for chapter-topic correspondence against the Ashtanga Hridaya by two blind, independent coders, with the Huangdi Neijing coded identically as a sham arm to measure generic premodern-medical overlap. The pre-registration fixed a reliability gate: the coding would support a percentage only if Cohen's κ reached 0.70. It returned κ = 0.68 (raw agreement 83.3%; all disagreements one-step boundary disputes). Under the registration, the pilot therefore dies: no correspondence percentage is claimed, the registered predictions were not scored, and the full-corpus audit does not proceed. The zombie 75% remains untraced and unusable — and, after this pilot, still unreplaced. The paper publishes the full record, including the passes' arithmetic explicitly labelled as unclaimed, because a gate that only fires in private is not a gate. Keywords: Gyushi; rGyud bzhi; Ashtanga Hridaya; Tibetan medicine; Ayurveda; zombie statistic; pre-registration; inter-rater reliability; registered report; negative result
